headline: The Fed gave the front end its cut and the long end sent the bill: 2s -3bp to 4.67% while 30s +7bp to 5.37% and breakevens pushed higher — a steepener for the wrong reason.
summary: Yesterday the question was what Powell would do with oil back above $100. Today we have the answer, and the curve told us what it thinks of it. The front end rallied — 2y -3bp to 4.67%, 3m bill -4bp to 4.18%, both down 25bp and 10bp on the month. The long end went the other way: 10y +6bp to 5.05%, 30y +7bp to 5.37%, 10y real +3bp to 2.67%. 2s10s steepened 9bp to 38bp, 3m10y +10bp to 87bp. TLT -0.8%. This is not a growth steepener; it is an inflation steepener. The 5y breakeven added 4bp to 2.49% and is +16bp on the month and turning up, the 10y breakeven 2.38%. The inflation composite deteriorated from -47 to -49, the single worst number on the board, and WTI did the deed: +2.2% to 102.07, +10.2% on the month, +77.8% YTD, with natural gas +11.9% in a session, DBC at the 97.5th percentile and oil/gold at the 95th. The 30-year mortgage is pinned at 7.32%, 94th percentile. Easing into that is a policy choice the bond market is charging for.

The risk plumbing, meanwhile, threw a party. VIX -3.5% to 16.91, the 20th percentile of its year; VIX3M -1.8% to 19.22 at the 15th; MOVE -3.4% to 94.55 and -7.1% on the month. The credit and vol composite leapt from +4 to +27, the biggest single-day composite change on the sheet, and the risk regime improved again to -10 from -15. Semis re-ripped for a third session: MU +5.9%, AMD +3.2%, AVGO +2.8%, SOXX +2.1%, SMH +1.7%, SMH/SPY +1.4% and turning up from a z=-1.2 month move. The Asia echo kept going — EWY +5.4%, KOSPI +3.1%, EWT +1.6% — and ORCL printed the move of the day at +10.7%, +11.9% on the week, from a base that is still -47.8% over twelve months. Speculative beta joined: SPHB/SPLV +2.0%, ARKK +1.6%, IPO +2.2%, EEM +1.6%, IBB +2.0%, XBI +1.7%. Credit never flinched — BKLN sits at the 98.8th percentile, HYG/IEF +0.3%.

What changed for the worse is the quality of the leadership, not its direction. Transports broke: DJT -2.5%, XTN -2.3%, IYT -1.7%, IYT/SPY -2.0% and sitting at the 17th percentile of the year. Housing re-cracked on the long-end move: DHI -2.7%, ITB -1.5%, XHB -1.2%, XHB/SPY at the 11th percentile. Breadth is deceptive — RSP/SPY posted the highest acceleration on the board at +2.46 and a z=1.47 month move, yet it fell 0.4% today and has rolled over. The factors accelerating hardest are all defensive: SPLV acceleration +2.16, USMV +1.76, MCD +2.58 on a +7.2% month, HD +2.2 on a +9.5% month, XLP z=1.37. A tape that rallies while low-vol and staples accelerate is a tape renting beta, not owning it. And the AI trade is rotating violently inside itself: as silicon rallied, the electricity leg came apart — ETN -8.9% on the month with acceleration -1.39, GEV -7.5%, NLR -7.7% at the 7.6th percentile, GRID -4.6%, VST -8.6% on the week. NVDA diverged from its own sector, -1.2%, and META is -14.4% on the month with acceleration -2.41 inside an XLC at the 0th percentile.

Two things to watch that nobody is paying for. First, liquidity: the TGA climbed another 3.1% to $1.0525tn, the 100th percentile of its year and +11.3% on the month, while RRP is functionally empty at $0.18bn — 92% below its 200-day. The drain has no sponge left, and the liquidity composite is a flat 0. Second, the dollar is only superficially softer. DXY -0.2% to 102.15 but still at the 93rd percentile; EURUSD 1.1156 at the 0th percentile of the year. Where it bites is LatAm: EWZ -2.0% today after -20.9% on the week, Bovespa -2.7% and -17.2% on the week, USDBRL +6.5% in five sessions, USDMXN at z=1.84 and the 96th percentile. And USD/KRW rose another 1.3% to 1341.6 on the very day Korea gained 5.4% — the same non-confirmation flagged yesterday, now two days old. Buy the equity bounce if you must, but the won is still telling you it is a squeeze, not an allocation.

good.text: Volatility broke on the decision: VIX -3.5% to 16.91 (20th percentile), VIX3M -1.8% to 19.22, MOVE -3.4% to 94.55 and -7.1% on the month. The credit and vol composite jumped from +4 to +27.
The front end finally got paid: 2y -3bp to 4.67% (-25bp on the month), 3m bill 4.18%, 2s10s +9bp to 38bp, 3m10y +10bp to 87bp. The flattening pressure that defined October has reversed.
Semis re-accelerated globally for a third session: MU +5.9%, AMD +3.2%, AVGO +2.8%, SOXX +2.1%, SMH/SPY +1.4% turning up from a z=-1.2 month move, EWY +5.4%, KOSPI +3.1%, EWT +1.6%.
Credit is not participating in any of the fear: BKLN at the 98.8th percentile, HYG/IEF +0.3%, HYG unchanged, LQD +2.0% on the month. There is no funding stress in this tape.
The speculative tail is bid, not bleeding: SPHB/SPLV +2.0%, ARKK +1.6%, IPO +2.2%, IBB +2.0%, XBI +1.7%, EEM +1.6%, and ORCL +10.7% off a 18th-percentile base.
Cyclical metals still confirm demand: copper +0.8% to 6.68 at the 93rd percentile, copper/gold +1.0% and sitting at the 100th percentile of its year, +26.6% YTD.

bad.text: The long end repriced through 5%: 10y +6bp to 5.05%, 30y +7bp to 5.37%, 10y real yield +3bp to 2.67%, 30-year mortgage 7.32% at the 94th percentile. Rates composite -35.

Inflation expectations rose into the easing: 5y breakeven +4bp to 2.49% and +16bp on the month, WTI +2.2% to 102.07, natgas +11.9% in a day, DBC at the 97.5th percentile, oil/gold at the 95th. Inflation composite -49, the worst on the board and deteriorating.
Transports failed outright: DJT -2.5%, XTN -2.3%, IYT -1.7%, IYT/SPY -2.0% and at the 17th percentile. The growth pulse of +7 rests on UPS and FDX, not on the freight complex.

Leadership turned defensive beneath a rising index: SPLV acceleration +2.16, USMV +1.76, MCD +2.58, HD +2.2, XLP z=1.37, while RSP/SPY fell 0.4% and rolled over despite the strongest acceleration on the sheet.

The AI electricity leg is coming apart while silicon rallies: ETN -8.9% on the month with acceleration -1.39, GEV -7.5%, NLR -7.7% at the 7.6th percentile, GRID -4.6%, VST -8.6% on the week, CEG at the 13th percentile.

LatAm and EM FX are where the dollar still bites: EWZ -2.0% after -20.9% on the week, Bovespa -17.2% weekly, USDBRL +6.5% in five sessions, USDMXN z=1.84 at the 96th percentile, and USD/KRW +1.3% to 1341.6 on a day Korea gained 5.4%.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener — short the long bond against the front end
trades.line: PAIR: short TLT vs long 2y — post-Fed inflation steepener
trades.expr: Short TLT (or Dec ultra-bond futures) against a duration-weighted long in 2y notes or SHY, roughly 4:1 by DV01. Options version: buy TLT Jan 78 puts financed by selling the 86 call.
trades.thesis: The Fed is easing into a live inflation impulse. The front end can rally on cuts; the long end has to absorb the breakeven, the supply and a TGA rebuild with no RRP buffer left. That is a one-way steepener until either oil rolls or the Fed re-hawks.
trades.trigger: Today the 10y rose 6bp to 5.05% and the 30y 7bp to 5.37% while the 2y fell 3bp to 4.67%. 2s10s +9bp to 38bp, 3m10y +10bp to 87bp. The 5y breakeven added 4bp to 2.49%, +16bp on the month and turning up. TLT -0.8% with trend state down. TGA $1.0525tn at the 100th percentile, RRP $0.18bn.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 28bp, or the 30y closing under 5.20% / TLT above 83.5 on a sustained basis — that would mean the long end has accepted the cut.

trades.name: Energy E&P over the index
trades.line: LONG XOP vs SPY: WTI $102, XOP +11.2% on the month
trades.expr: Long XOP against an equal-dollar SPY short; core single names XOM and CVX for lower beta. Add OIH for the services kicker.
trades.thesis: Oil is the macro driver this quarter and energy equity has only partially caught it. Energy is the only sector with positive relative strength on both the 1m and 3m windows and a trend state of up.
trades.trigger: WTI +2.2% to 102.07, +10.2% on the month, +77.8% YTD; DBC at the 97.5th percentile; XLE relative strength +9.3% 1m and +10.6% 3m with trend up; XOP +11.2% on the month with rs +10.3%/+10.2%; XOM +12.0% on the month at z=1.18 and the 96.6th percentile; CVX +11.1%.
trades.stop: WTI closing below $92 (that is the 200-day region), or XLE relative strength rolling over to down for two consecutive weeks / XOP below 180.
trades.target: XOP 230, roughly 12-15% of relative outperformance versus SPY.

trades.name: Short home construction into a 5% ten-year
trades.line: SHORT ITB: 10y at 5.05%, mortgage 7.32% at 94th pctile
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan 85 puts. Beta-neutral version: short ITB against long XLV.
trades.thesis: Housing cannot clear at a 7.32% mortgage, and the long end just made it worse on the very day the Fed cut. The group has already lost the 200-day and is making new relative lows — the cut is not the rescue the bulls priced.
trades.trigger: ITB -1.5%, XHB -1.2%, DHI -2.7% today while the 10y rose 6bp to 5.05% and the 30y 7bp to 5.37%. Mortgage 7.32%, +37bp on the month, 94th percentile, z=1.1. XHB/SPY at the 11th percentile; ITB 6.8% below its 200-day and -13.1% over twelve months.
trades.stop: 10y back under 4.85%, or ITB reclaiming 94 and its 200-day.

trades.name: Silicon over electrons
trades.line: PAIR: long SMH vs short GEV/ETN/NLR power basket
trades.expr: Long SMH against an equal-dollar short basket of GEV, ETN and NLR (optionally add GRID and VST), roughly 1:1 notional.
trades.thesis: The AI capex dollar is rotating out of the power build-out and back into the chips. The electricity complex is making 52-week lows with negative acceleration while semis are re-accelerating off a washout — the same money, a different leg.
trades.trigger: SMH +1.7%, SOXX +2.1%, MU +5.9%, AMD +3.2%, AVGO +2.8%, SMH/SPY +1.4% and turning up from a z=-1.2 month move. Against that: ETN -8.9% on the month with acceleration -1.39, GEV -7.5% and -1.9% today, NLR -7.7% at the 7.6th percentile, GRID -4.6%, VST -8.6% on the week, CEG at the 13th percentile.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY back below 0.70, or the power basket outperforming SMH for two straight weeks. NVDA, already -1.2% today and diverging from its sector, breaking its 200-day would also kill this.

trades.name: Steepener equity expression: banks over bond proxies
trades.line: PAIR: long XLF vs short XLU — curve beats the yield proxy
trades.expr: Long XLF (add KRE for more curve beta) against an equal-dollar XLU short.
trades.thesis: A 38bp 2s10s that just steepened 9bp is net income for banks and a discount-rate problem for utilities. Utilities have rallied 8.3% on the month on a z=1.58 move with acceleration +2.15 while the trend state is still down and 3m relative strength is -10.2% — that is a crowded defensive bid about to meet a 5.37% thirty-year.
trades.trigger: 2s10s +9bp to 38bp; XLU -0.8% today, trend down, 2.95% below its 200-day despite the month-long bounce; XLF +0.4% with relative strength +2.7% 1m and acceleration +1.34; XLI/XLU +1.2% today and turning up from a z=-1.81 month move; JPM +1.0%, GS +1.5%.
trades.stop: 2s10s re-flattening below 28bp, or XLU closing above its 200-day for a week.

trades.name: Buy convexity while it is on sale
trades.line: LONG vol: VIX 16.9 at 20th pctile, SKEW 148.7 turning up
trades.expr: Buy a Dec SPX 2%-out by 8%-out put spread financed by selling a 4% call, or a Dec VIX 20/28 call spread. Size as a hedge, not a view.
trades.thesis: The index is within 6.1% of its 200-day extension at the 95th percentile of the year, but internals are deteriorating and the long bond just repriced. Paying 16.9 vol for protection against an inflation-steepener accident is the cheapest line item on this sheet.
trades.trigger: VIX -3.5% to 16.91, the 19.6th percentile; VIX3M 19.22 at the 15th; term structure 0.88 in full contango. Meanwhile SKEW 148.74 and turning up, RSP/SPY -0.4% and rolling over, IWM/SPY at the 23rd percentile, and the 10y at 5.05%.
trades.stop: VIX sustaining below 14 with RSP/SPY re-accelerating and the 10y back under 4.85% — then the melt-up is real and you pay the premium.

trades.name: Health care and biotech as the new defensive growth
trades.line: LONG IBB + XLV: rs turning up, XLV at 96th pctile
trades.expr: Long IBB as the core with an XLV overlay; relative version is long IBB against short XLC, which sits at the 0th percentile with -11.0% 3m relative strength.
trades.thesis: If the market wants defense, this is the only defensive group with earnings growth and upward relative strength rather than a crowded bond-proxy bid. It also carries zero oil and zero duration sensitivity, which is what today's tape penalised.
trades.trigger: IBB +2.0% today at the 99th percentile with relative strength +1.8% 1m and +8.1% 3m and trend up; XBI +1.7% and +3.1% on the week; XLV +4.9% on the month at z=1.06, 96th percentile, relative strength turning up; LLY +8.7% on the month, UNH +7.7%, IHI +5.2% with acceleration +1.43.
trades.stop: IBB below 200, or XLV relative strength rolling back to down and the sector losing its 200-day.
trades.target: IBB 240; XLV continuing to add 4-6% of relative performance.
